title: Tanzanian Kachori
community: Zanzibar and coastal Tanzania — Indian Ocean pastry tradition
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Kachori — crispy, slightly puffed round pastries filled with spiced lentils or peas, deep-fried until golden. The Indian Ocean's contribution to Tanzania's street food — a round, satisfying pastry that appears in the urojo bowl and at every Zanzibar market.
longDesc: Kachori arrived on the Tanzanian coast through the Indian Ocean trade and became a permanent part of Zanzibar's street food landscape — the round, crispy pastry filled with spiced dal that appears in the urojo bowl and is sold independently at every market.
ingredients: 1 cup yellow split peas or lentils — soaked and cooked
steps: Make filling: cook onion until golden. Add spices, cooked lentils. Mash partially. Add coriander. Cool completely.
Make pastry: rub oil into flour and salt. Add water gradually to a stiff dough. Knead 5 minutes.
Divide dough into 12 balls. Flatten each into a 8cm round.
Place 1 tbsp filling in the centre. Gather edges and pinch firmly to seal.
Fry at 170°C for 4—5 minutes until golden and slightly puffed.
chefTips: The seal must be completely airtight — any gap and the filling escapes into the oil.
The stiff dough is intentional — it holds its shape during frying.
cookingScience: Kachori puffs during frying because the moisture in the filling converts to steam as the oil temperature rises. This steam, trapped by the sealed dough, creates internal pressure that puffs the pastry. The dough must be stiff enough to withstand this pressure without bursting.
sustainabilityTips: Lentils and peas — nitrogen-fixing legume filling.
storage: Freeze uncooked 2 months. Fry from frozen.
culturalNote: Kachori is the Indian Ocean's most travelled pastry — it arrived in Zanzibar on trading dhows and never left. It is now as Zanzibari as the cloves that grow on the island.
